summary: The Last Shift is a seven-slide story presentation for young readers about two NASA machines left on other worlds: the Apollo Lunar Module descent stage and the Mars Pathfinder lander with its Sojourner rover. Through two short, imagined mission diaries, readers learn why the hardware stayed, what it helped astronauts or scientists accomplish, and how each mission ended. Factual captions and NASA source links are kept separate from the storytelling voice. The project introduces engineering choices, planetary exploration, and scientific legacy in an accessible way. The current project artifact is the seven-slide presentation; it is not a separate educational app.
details:
The Last Shift is a story presentation for school-age space enthusiasts, approximately 10–14. It follows two different mission endings. At the Apollo landing sites, the Lunar Module’s descent stage remained on the Moon after serving as the landing platform, carrying supplies, and supporting the crew’s return to lunar orbit. On Mars, Sojourner explored with the Pathfinder lander acting as its communications relay. NASA JPL reports that the lander’s power-system failure ended the relay and rover operations.

The presentation pairs a brief first-person diary voice with factual captions and mission timelines. The diary voice is an imaginative storytelling device, not a historical quotation. The goal is to help young readers connect mission hardware to the science and engineering it enabled.

The current project is a seven-slide HTML presentation made with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It has on-screen and keyboard navigation. It does not include a separate deployed website, interactive map, or educational app. OpenAI ChatGPT assisted with drafting the text and generating presentation code. The team is responsible for reviewing the facts and final wording. No AI-generated images, video, or audio are used.
